title.narrative: West Kalimantan Power Grid Strengthening Project

description.narrative: The proposed project is perfectly aligned with ADB's Energy Sector Assessment Strategy and Roadmap, which supports investment in strategic transmission assets that connects regions or countries across seas or international boundaries to optimize power networks by reducing the overall need for reserve capacity, improving system reliability, removing transmission bottlenecks, and transmitting cheaper power from one area to the other, addressing overall regional socio-economic and environmental improvement.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Cost of operating West Kalimantan power system reduced

In West Kalimantan, PLN's average cost of generation reduced to $0.18/kWh (2009 baseline: $0.25/kWh) Achievement: 0.07 Progress/Status: As of 30 September 2020, West Kalimantan (Khatulistiwa System, interconnected with SESCO) average cost of generation is IDR 1,105/kWh (from IDR 1,142/kWh in July 2020) = $0.07/kWh (ADB exchange rate as of 30 September 2020, USD 1 = IDR14,869). The decrease in generation cost is because the costly diesel power plants are gradually decreased by end of 2018, West Kalimantan mainly relies on coal and imported energy from Sarawak Data Source: Electricity statistics published by PLN

Power interconnection capacity of 230 MW established Achievement: 208.8 Progress/Status: • As of 30 September 2020, average actual power import is 159.93MW during off-peak hours and 208.76MW during peak hours. Average power import reached 230MW up to 245.4 MW (peak hours) from October 2017 to May 2020. • 5th Amendment of PEA will be signed in December 2020 and applied in 2021. It regulates electricity purchase from SESCO with nominated capacity of peak/off-peak hours 110/80 MW. • Coal power plant projects from previous government's electricity generation Fast Tack Program (FTP) 1 and FTP2 are now completed or being constructed. The price of coal is IDR 900/kWh, while the import price is MYR 32.32 cent/kWh (IDR 1,156/kWh, based on ADB forex as of 30 September 2020). This reduces the need of imported power. • Future power import targets are decreased in PEA and RUPTL 2018-2027. The interconnected grid will continue to contribute in ensuring Khatulistiwa grid reliability and stability, with potential two-way power purchase agreements (export and import) to Sarawak. Based on RUPTL 2019-2028, the Khatulistiwa grid is planned to be interconnected to Barito Mahakam grid of Central/South Kalimantan. Data Source: PLN's Annual Reports
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: New connections to households in West Kalimantan Indicator: About 8,000 new households connected to electricity network (2010 baseline: 518,412) Achievement: 1730 Progress/Status: As of 30 September 2020, 1,730 households connected to ADB 52.973 km medium voltage (MV) and 46.760 km low voltage (LV) lines. PLN to assess possibility to increase household connection. Data Source: - report from Unit Induk Wilayah (UIW)

Output: Construction of Sarawak-West Kalimantan interconnection network Indicator: 275/150/20 kV substation in Bengkayang completed by 2014 Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Bengkayang substation is fully constructed and energized.
150/20kV Bengkayang SS financed by PLN completed in May 2016. Data Source: Project progress reports, consultant's reports, and ADB team's site inspection reports

Output: Construction of Sarawak-West Kalimantan interconnection network Indicator: About 83 km of 275 kV double-circuit transmission line between Bengkayang and the Sarawak border completed by 2014 Achievement: 81.375 Progress/Status: 81.375 km of 275kV TL double circuit transmission line from Sarawak border to Bengkayang is now fully constructed. First and second circuits were energized on 20 January 2016 and 19 May 2016 respectively. Data Source: Project progress reports, consultant's reports, and ADB team's site inspection reports

Output: Construction of new transmission network in West Kalimantan (Bengkayang-Ngabang-Tayan) Indicator: 150/20 kV substation in Ngabang and four-line feeder extension in 150 kV Tayan substation and Bengkayang substation completed by 2015 Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: 150/20 kV substation in Ngabang and four-line feeder extension in 150 kV Tayan substation and Bengkayang substation fully energized in November 2017 Data Source: - Project progress reports and consultant's reports - ADB team's site inspection reports

Output: Construction of new transmission network in West Kalimantan (Bengkayang-Ngabang-Tayan) Indicator: About 145 km of 150 kV double-circuit transmission line between Bengkayang-Ngabang-Tayan completed by 2015 Achievement: 144.65 Progress/Status: 144.65 km of 150 kV double-circuit transmission line between Bengkayang-Ngabang-Tayan fully energized in June 2018 Data Source: - Project progress reports and consultant's reports - ADB team's site inspection reports

Output: Construction of new transmission network in West Kalimantan (Tayan-Sanggau-Sekadau) Indicator: 150/20 kV substation in Sanggau and Sekadau and extension of 150 kV Tayan substation completed by 2018. Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Construction of P5 (substations) as of 30 September 2020 = 94.53%. Tayan SS 98.77%, Sanggau SS 88.86%, Sekadau SS 95.75%. Physical completion for Tayan SS is completed, CC to be issued by November 2020. Target for Sanggau and Sekadau SS: - physical completion by July 2021 - point to point test by June 2021 (Sanggau and Sekadau SS through P7) Data Source: - Project progress reports and consultant's reports - ADB team's site inspection reports

Output: Construction of new transmission network in West Kalimantan (Tayan-Sanggau-Sekadau) Indicator: About 119.43 km of 150 kV double-circuit transmission line between Tayan-Sanggau-Sekadau completed by 2018. Achievement: 94.38 Progress/Status: Construction of P6 (Tayan-Sanggau TL) as of 30 September 2020 = 97.92%. Commissioning was completed in October 2020. CC to be issued by November 2020.
Construction of P7 (Sanggau-Sekadau TL) as of 30 September 2020 = 69.87%. Target for commissioning by July 2021. Physical completion target in July 2021 Data Source: - Project progress reports and consultant's reports - ADB team's site inspection reports
